title: Hard Issue, Weak Model, or Bad Run? Rethinking Failure Prediction for Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.08285v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Trajectory-based failure predictors for software engineering (SE) agents read the partial trajectory of a run to flag whether it is going right or wrong. If it is going wrong, the run can be stopped, retried, or switched to another model. We ask whether these predictors learn anything about the run itself. On public SWE-bench Verified trajectories, where each model attempts each issue once, two run-independent factors dominate predictor performance. The first is issue difficulty: a reference score that never looks at the run, only at how hard the issue is for other models, reaches 0.92 AUROC, whereas trajectory predictors reach about 0.62. The second is model ability: within an issue, knowing which model ran predicts failure better than our predictors do, and the predictors largely reproduce the overall ability ranking of the models. translated_title: 难题、弱模型，还是糟糕的一次运行？重新思考编码智能体的失败预测
translated_abstract: 针对软件工程（SE）智能体的基于轨迹的失败预测器会读取一次运行的部分轨迹，以判断该运行是朝着正确还是错误的方向发展。如果运行出现问题，可以停止、重试该运行，或切换到另一个模型。我们探究这些预测器是否真正从运行本身学到了任何东西。在公开的 SWE-bench Verified 轨迹数据上（其中每个模型对每个问题只尝试一次），两个与运行无关的因素主导了预测器的性能。第一个是问题难度：一个从不查看运行内容、仅参考该问题对其他模型有多难的基准分数，达到了 0.92 的 AUROC，而轨迹预测器只能达到约 0.62。第二个是模型能力：在同一个问题内，仅知道是哪个模型在运行就比我们的预测器更能预测失败，而且这些预测器在很大程度上只是复现了模型的整体能力排名。除了难度和能力之外，预测器从轨迹中获得的信息在统计上等同于零……
tldr: 该研究发现在 SWE-bench Verified 上，轨迹失败预测器的性能主要由问题难度和模型能力这两个与运行无关的因素决定，其从轨迹本身获得的信号在统计上几乎为零，从而质疑了此类预测器真正学到运行相关信息的假设。
en_tdlr: On SWE-bench Verified, trajectory-based failure predictors for coding agents are dominated by two run-independent factors—issue difficulty and model ability—and gain statistically negligible signal from the trajectory itself, challenging the premise that such predictors learn anything about the run.
